course_title: Language Awareness & Cross-Cultural Competence for the Global Workplace
course_description: Digital tools and innovation are changing the way we communicate at work with people around the world. At the same time workplaces both in Australia and overseas are becoming increasingly multilingual and multicultural. This course will introduce you to how language works in this context and the critical role it plays in communication, alongside understanding how the ways in which language is used are central to building relationships and trust in different cultural settings. It will help you develop the cross-cultural skills you need to thrive in an increasingly globalised workplace from an Australian point of view.

course_aims:
This course aims to enhance your understanding of how we as communicators build relationships and effective communication, and use language, which marginalises others. When we communicate with others, many factors are at play. These include the ways that languages and the norms of interaction are structured, the cultural practices of speakers and communities, and attitudes towards situations, languages and their speakers.

In this course, you will gather skills to recognise and relate these factors to communication. In doing so, you will develop the capacity to communicate effectively and appropriately with people from diverse cultural backgrounds in global communication.

learning_outcomes.description: Recognise the ways in which language in communication is used to build relationships and trust, and to exclude and marginalise.
Effectively apply verbal and non-verbal language and communication knowledge and skills to intercultural communication contexts
Effectively apply theories and concepts in analysing communication, identify problems and provide solutions.

Critically reflect upon your view of communication and its influence on interaction to demonstrate your adaptability and responsibility as an effective communicator in increasingly globalised and culturally diverse workplaces.

assessment_details.task_description: In the Week 13 tutorial, each student will be given examples of real workplace communication. Students are required to analyse the interaction between participants, identify key issues and topics, and provide informed recommendations based on concepts and frameworks studied in COMU2040. Each student will have: 5 minutes to read the provided material and make notes 5 minutes to present their analysis Students will be assessed individually based on the following criteria: Application of course concepts Demonstrates the ability to analyse workplace communication using relevant theories, concepts, and tools covered in the course. Identification of communication issues Identifies and critically evaluates problems or breakdowns in the interaction within a workplace communication context. Quality of recommendations Provides clear, relevant, and practical recommendations informed by course content and tailored to the specific workplace context presented in the example.
